title: Strict open-tensor systems realize the completion-unit-normalized open map
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=A/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, with small pro-etale sites and $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use unbounded module derived categories, exact localized open extension/restriction $j_!\dashv j^*$ with identity open unit, and the unit-normalized ordinary tensor map $\gamma^o:j_!K\otimes^L_{R_V}N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes^L_{R_U}j^*N)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Let $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ be strict semilinear reduction/total-limit with actual unit $u$ and counit $e$, and let $J$ denote exact system open extension [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use quotient/Koszul completion $C_W$ with unit $\eta_W$, completed tensor $\widehat\otimes$, and completed restriction, canonically identified with $j^*$ on complete objects [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector, lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence, def-pur-integral-derived-operations, lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison].

For any complete $K\in D(R_U)$ and $N\in D(R_V)$ put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_U}(A_n)_U$ and $N_n=N\otimes^L_{R_V}(A_n)_V$. In the derived category of whole semilinear systems put
$$T=\bigl((j_!K)_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_V}N_n\bigr)_n,\qquad S=\bigl(K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_U}j^*N_n\bigr)_n.$$
Use their canonical quotient transitions and the strict open-reduction comparison $r_j$ [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. The system tensor map $\gamma_\bullet:T\xrightarrow{\sim}JS$ is the simultaneous unit-normalized open tensor map after $r_j$. Its normalization is fixed on flat-term K-flat quotient representatives: it carries the strict tensor quotient augmentation of $H=j_!K\otimes^L_{R_V}N$ to $J$ of that of $H_U=K\otimes^L_{R_U}j^*N$ after $\gamma^o$, as an equality of augmented strict system maps.

There is a unique completed open tensor isomorphism
$$\gamma^c:j_!K\widehat\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\widehat\otimes j^*N)$$
characterized by
$$\gamma^c\circ\eta_{V,H}=j_!(\eta_{U,H_U})\circ\gamma^o.$$
Under the specified substitution identification $\mathcal L_VT\cong j_!K\widehat\otimes N$ and the target identification $\mathcal L_VJS\cong j_!(K\widehat\otimes j^*N)$ obtained from $r_j$, its actual unit $u_{j_!(-)}$ and the coherent counit $e_S$, one has
$$\mathcal L_V(\gamma_\bullet)=\gamma^c.$$
The identifications are those of [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], applied to the entire systems. After the open unit and restriction/tensor identifications, $j^*\gamma^c$ is the identity. These identities retain quotient transitions and augmentations before total limit. They do not assert that individual finite derived evaluations are faithful. No finite-type, constructibility, boundedness or finite-Tor condition on $K,N$ is required.

proof.text: The open reduction-tensor comparison is an isomorphism from the reduction of the ordinary open tensor to S. Reduction of any object is normalized, and normalization is invariant under an isomorphism (conjugate the defining Hom-bijections). Normalized reconstruction therefore makes M=L_U S complete and the actual counit e_S invertible. Form gamma_c by sourceIdentification, L_V(systemMap gamma), and targetIdentification. All these factors are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Set a_U=eta_U followed by openIdentification. Counit naturality and the left triangle identity give R_U(a_U)=q_U followed by e_S inverse. Naturality of strictOpen.r at a_U, sameOpen at complete M, dFormula, and unitXHom imply u_(j_!H_U) followed by L_V(r_H_U J(R_U(a_U))) and d_M is j_!(a_U). Expand the defining source/system/target maps, cancel q_V against its inverse, and use unit naturality at gamma. The preceding identity then gives gamma_c after eta_V equal to gamma followed by j_!eta_U.

proof.text: For any X, R(unit_X) is invertible: its composite with the counit at R(X) is identity by the left triangle, and that counit is invertible by normalized reconstruction. For complete Y, unit_Y is invertible. If two maps completion(X)→Y agree after eta_X, transport along completionV/U, apply R, and cancel R(unit_X). Naturality and cancellation of unit_Y then give equality of the original maps. The target of gamma_c is complete by extensionComplete and invariance of completeness under openIdentification. Thus gamma_c is unique from the completion-unit equation.

proof.text: Restrict the completion-unit equation. Cancel restrictionCompletion inverse and use the just-proved completion Hom-injectivity on U. The restrictionUnit square and naturality of completionUnit reduce the desired identity to naturality of the inverse open unit at eta_U. This proves exactly restrictedIdentification. The realization identity holds by the definition of gamma_c. No equality is detected by finite derived evaluations and completeness of the two original tensor inputs is unnecessary for this part of the argument.

Step-by-step: Step 1 builds q_V and q_U from flat-term K-flat models (lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback) by an elementary balanced isomorphism. For Step 3, η=u holds by the open-quotient Koszul completeness lemma (c∘κ=u) and the constant-completion equivalence, whose Koszul tower is the same as the reflector's. Step 4 gets γ^c from the reflector's Hom bijections; j_! preserves completeness because j is quasi-compact, and restriction preserves it by the immersion comparison. In Step 5 the types of b_S = d_j(M) L_V J(e_S^{-1}) check, and e_S is invertible by the reconstruction calculus. I verified the counit/triangle calculation of Step 6, the (**) cancellation of Step 7 (only u at the complete j_!M is inverted), and the reflector-injectivity argument g=γ^c of Step 8 symbol by symbol. Step 9 is condensed but each implication is a cited statement. I confirmed it independently by applying j^* to the characterizing equation. Edge cases checked: j=id, U empty, K or N = 0, and t-torsion inputs with higher Tor. All 12 off-unit tools are declared in tool_uses and accepted as generic. Two minor points need no fix: Step 5 says 'Step 1' where it means Steps 1 and 3, and r_j of the semilinear model and of the integral comparison are the same representative construction.
